text: This is the hands-on core of the chapter — the actual patterns you'll reuse for every check you ever write.
Every check session starts the same way. Connect, Database Engine, point it at the right server.
Then a New Query window, opened against that connection — right-click the server, or use the toolbar button. This is where every check gets written.

Nearly every check has the same shape: select the key columns, from the table, where the condition is true only when the row is bad. Build the habit early — write the WHERE clause for the failure, not the success. You're not selecting good rows, you're hunting the ones that need attention.
Click Execute, or press F5, and the check runs against the connected database — exactly the same way any other query would.

One check is useful once. A failures report — every rule's violations in a single result set, labeled by which rule fired — is what you actually want to run daily. UNION ALL stitches multiple rules into one scannable list.
This is what that combined report looks like once it comes back — one row per violation, labeled by rule, in a plain SSMS results grid.

Keep checks read-only — never update or delete inside a check. Write SARGable WHERE clauses so the engine can actually use your indexes. Cast keys consistently across UNION branches. And once these are automated, schedule the heavy ones outside business hours.
You now have the full pattern: connect, write, run, combine. Next up: referential integrity checks — the specific pattern for catching orphaned rows between related tables.
